```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center",
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

This guide extends the introductory vignette (`vignettes/FLicc_intro_vignette.Rmd`).
It covers the full single-stock workflow, the model options added in FLicc 1.0.9 and
1.0.10, and practical recommendations from simulation testing: fishing mortality
over time, tail treatment of the length compositions, reference points and
steepness, Monte-Carlo ensembles, and use inside a management strategy
evaluation (MSE).

# Installation

`FLicc` depends on `FLCore`, `ggplotFL` and `TMB`. On Windows, compiling the TMB
model requires Rtools (<https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/>).

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("TMB", type = "source")
install.packages(c("FLCore", "ggplotFL"),
                 repos = c("https://flr.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
remotes::install_github("henning-winker/FLicc")                    # release
remotes::install_github("henning-winker/FLicc", ref = "dev-merge")  # development
```

```{r load}
library(FLicc)
packageVersion("FLicc")
```

# Workflow overview

1. Prepare length-frequency data (LFD) by gear as `FLQuants`.
2. Specify life-history parameters (`FLPar`) and build an `FLStockLen` with `stocklen()`.
3. Fit the model with `fiticc()`.
4. Check convergence and the fit to the length compositions.
5. Read status (SPR) and reference points; derive length-based indicators and advice plots.
6. Propagate life-history uncertainty with `mc_flicc()`; use `flicc.sa()` inside an MSE.

**Rapid defaults.** A plain `fiticc()` call uses the GTG population model, a
multinomial likelihood, fixed growth (Linf, CVL) and natural mortality, and a
random walk on log F with its standard deviation fixed at `sigmaF = 0.3`.
These defaults are fast and stable; every other option in this guide is a
deliberate departure from them.

# Length-frequency data

```{r data}
data("alfonsino")
lfd <- FLQuantLen(lfd_long_to_wide(as.data.frame(lfd_alfonsino)), unit = "cm", midL = FALSE)
names(lfd)
range(as.numeric(dimnames(lfd[[1]])$len)); range(as.numeric(dimnames(lfd[[1]])$year))
```

`midL = FALSE` means the length values are lower bin boundaries. A long table
(`as.data.frame()`) is the easiest way to check length, year and gear structure.

```{r plot-lfd}
plot_lfd(lfd, type = "relmax")
```

## Effective sample size

Length samples are usually clustered (trips, hauls), so raw counts overstate the
information. `lfdess()` rescales each gear to an effective sample size without
changing the proportions:

```{r ess}
lfd.ess <- lfdess(lfd, ess.g = c(Trawl = 250, Gillnet = 350))
```

# Life history and the stock object

```{r lhpar}
lhpar <- FLPar(linf = 55.7, k = 0.08, M = 0.162, L50 = 31.1859,
               a = 0.004721956 / 1000, b = 3.146168)
stklen <- stocklen(lfd, lhpar, m_model = "constant")
```

- `linf`, `k`: von Bertalanffy growth; `M`: natural mortality (M/k is what the
  length model uses); `L50` (and optionally `L95`): maturity at length; `a`, `b`:
  weight at length, $W(L) = aL^b$.
- `m_model`: `"constant"`, `"inverse"`, `"Lorenzen"` or `"Gislason"` for M at
  length.

```{r plot-lh, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_mat(stklen)
plot_m(FLStocks(lapply(setNames(nm = c("constant", "Lorenzen")),
                       function(m) stocklen(lfd, lhpar, m_model = m))))
```

# Model

## Fishing mortality and selectivity

For gear $g$ in year $y$, $F_{g,y}(L) = F_{g,y} S_g(L)$ with selectivity scaled to a
maximum of one, $Z_y(L) = M(L) + \sum_g F_{g,y}(L)$. Selectivity per gear
(`sel_fun`): `"logistic"`, `"dsnormal"` (dome, double-sided normal) or
`"normal"`. Gear shares of F are informed by `catch_by_gear` (relative catch by
gear; a numeric vector or `FLQuants` by year).

## Population model

`pop_model = "gtg"` (default) follows LBSPR: growth-type groups with
$L_{\infty,h} = L_\infty(1 + \mathrm{CVL}\, z_h)$, $z_h$ on
`seq(-maxsd, maxsd, length = ngtg)` (defaults 13 groups, `maxsd = 2`), and
survival across bin $i$ for group $h$

$$
N_{i+1,h} = N_{i,h}\left(\frac{L_{\infty,h} - L_{i+1}}{L_{\infty,h} - L_i}\right)^{Z_i/k}.
$$

`pop_model = "gamma"` follows fishblicc (gamma-distributed Linf, numerical
integration; slower).

Both are **equilibrium** models: each year's composition is explained by the
equilibrium at that year's F. When F changes, the large fish adjust slowly, so the
estimated SPR lags behind (see section 8).

## Observation model

`obs_model`: `"mn"` multinomial (default), `"nb"` negative binomial, `"dm"`
Dirichlet-multinomial (overdispersed compositions; the effective sample size sets
the precision).

## Status: SPR

$$
\mathrm{SPR}_y = \frac{\sum_L N_{F_y}(L) W(L) P_{mat}(L)}{\sum_L N_0(L) W(L) P_{mat}(L)},
$$

spawning output per recruit at the year's F relative to unfished. SPR is the
quantity length data can identify; it equals $B/B_0$ only when recruitment does
not depend on stock size (see section 9.2).

# Fitting

```{r fit}
t0 <- system.time(
  fit <- fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"),
                catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3), settings = list(CVL = 0.1))
)
t0[["elapsed"]]
sigmaF_flicc(fit)        # 0.3: fixed by default
```

Main arguments: `lfd`, `stklen`, `sel_fun` (one per gear), `catch_by_gear`,
`settings` (below), `n_restart` (optimiser restarts if the gradient is large),
`se` (standard errors; `FALSE` skips `sdreport()` for speed), `start` (restart
from previous estimates, e.g. `fit$opt$par`).

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `pop_model` | `"gtg"` | `"gtg"`, `"gamma"` (and `"gtg.dyn"`, development) |
| `obs_model` | `"mn"` | `"mn"`, `"nb"`, `"dm"` |
| `CVL` | 0.1 | CV of Linf among growth groups (fixed unless `CVL.sd`) |
| `ngtg`, `maxsd` | 13, 2 | GTG grid (as LBSPR) |
| `Mpow` | 0 | M/K at length $\propto (L_\infty/L)^{Mpow}$ |
| `linf.sd`, `Mk.sd`, `CVL.sd` | `NULL` | estimate with a prior around the input |
| `sigmaF` | 0.3 | random-walk SD of log F, fixed |
| `prior_sigmaF` | – | `c(mean, sd, use)`: estimate sigmaF with a prior; `FALSE`: no random walk |
| `F_re` | `FALSE` | log F as random effects (Laplace), sigmaF estimated |
| `tail_cut` | `NULL` | exclude bins with lower bound `>= tail_cut` (length) |
| `Lplus` | `NULL` | pool bins with lower bound `>= Lplus` |
| `rob_eps` | 0 | robust likelihood: `p = (1 - eps) p + eps / nbins` |
| `spr_ref` | 40 | SPR target(s) (%) whose Fspr is stored with the fit |
| `tail_warning` | `FALSE` | warn about fish beyond the largest GTG Linf |

## Convergence and fit diagnostics

```{r convergence}
flicc_convergence(fit)
AIC(LLflicc(fit))
```

```{r diag-plots}
plot_len(fit, by_gear = TRUE, year = 2022:2024)
plot_sel(fit)
plot_spr(fit, ci = TRUE)
```

`plot_spr(ci = TRUE)` adds 95% intervals from the standard errors of log SPR
(`spr_ci_flicc()`); several fits can be compared with a named list.

# Fishing mortality over time

Log F by gear follows a random walk, $\log F_{y} = \log F_{y-1} + \varepsilon_y$,
$\varepsilon_y \sim N(0, \sigma_F^2)$. It links the years, so selectivity and F are
estimated jointly from all compositions, and it bridges years or gears without
data. The options differ only in how $\sigma_F$ is treated:

| Option | Settings | sigmaF | Speed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixed (default) | `sigmaF = 0.3` | fixed | fast | recommended routine and MSE choice |
| penalised with prior | `prior_sigmaF = c(log(0.5), 0.3, 1)` | estimated | fast | earlier default; pulled towards small values |
| random effects | `F_re = TRUE` | estimated (marginal likelihood) | ~5-10x slower | SEs include the F process; weak prior `c(log(0.3), 0.5, 1)` unless given |
| no random walk | `prior_sigmaF = FALSE` | – | fast | each year free (LBSPR-like, shared selectivity); fails for years without data |
| separate years | `by_year = TRUE` | – | fast | independent fits incl. selectivity |

```{r f-options}
fits_F <- list(
  fixed_0.3 = fit,
  prior     = fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                     settings = list(CVL = 0.1, prior_sigmaF = c(log(0.5), 0.3, 1))),
  F_re      = fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                     settings = list(CVL = 0.1, F_re = TRUE)),
  no_RW     = fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                     settings = list(CVL = 0.1, prior_sigmaF = FALSE))
)
sapply(fits_F, sigmaF_flicc)
plot_spr(fits_F, ci = TRUE)
```

**Avoid** estimating sigmaF without a prior as a penalised fixed effect
(`prior_sigmaF = c(NA, NA, 1)`): every random-walk step rewards a smaller sigmaF,
it collapses towards 0 and F becomes flat. FLicc warns in that case.

**Estimate once, then fix.** For repeated fits (MSE, ensembles), estimate sigmaF
once with `F_re = TRUE` on the full data and fix it:

```{r f-fix}
sig <- sigmaF_flicc(fits_F$F_re)
sig
fit_sig <- fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                  settings = list(CVL = 0.1, sigmaF = sig), se = FALSE)
```

## Lag under changing F (simulation results)

In simulations with an alfonsino-like operating model (fixed-CV length-at-age,
annual recruitment, Beverton-Holt h = 0.75, two gears, realistic two-stage
sampling), the equilibrium model follows a change in F only partly: during a
rebuild the estimated SPR trend was 14% of the true trend with sigmaF estimated
(collapsing), about 27% with sigmaF fixed at 0.3, and about 30% without a random
walk. The smoothing lag of the random walk is therefore largely removed at
sigmaF = 0.3; larger values or no random walk add little responsiveness but more
year-to-year noise (+10 to +50%). The remaining lag comes from the data: the
largest fish carry the longest memory of past F. A tail cut (next section)
roughly doubles the responsiveness.

# Tail of the length composition

The largest fish are the most sensitive part of the composition: to Linf, to the
growth variability CVL, to dome-shaped selectivity or lower availability of big
fish, to the GTG discretisation, and to past F. Three options reduce their
influence.

## Tail cut (`tail_cut`)

`tail_cut = L` excludes bins with lower bound $\geq L$ from the likelihood. Observed
and predicted compositions are both truncated and the predictions renormalised:

$$
p_{l \mid L < L_{cut}} = \frac{p_l}{\sum_{l' : L_{l'} < L_{cut}} p_{l'}}.
$$

This is exact conditioning: the model still describes the whole population with
its input CVL, and SPR and reference points use all lengths. No adjustment of CVL
is needed. `tail_cut` is an **absolute length** (as `Lplus`), so the same bins are
used whatever Linf is assumed in sensitivity runs or ensemble draws. (Values
<= 1.5 are read as a fraction of Linf, with a warning, for older scripts.)

```{r tailcut}
fit_cut <- fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                  settings = list(CVL = 0.1, tail_cut = 47))       # ~0.85 x Linf
fit_cut$tmb_data$LLB[fit_cut$tmb_data$cut_bin + 1]               # first excluded bin
plot_spr(list(no_cut = fit, cut_47 = fit_cut), ci = TRUE)
```

Simulation results (alfonsino-like OM, stable F, correct Linf):

| Effect of a cut at 0.80-0.85 x Linf | no cut | with cut |
|---|---|---|
| CVL input 0.07 / 0.10 / 0.13 (true 0.1): SPR bias | +9 / -1 / -11% | +13 / +9 / +4% |
| strong dome on one gear (fitted as logistic) | -17% | +1% |
| responsiveness during a rebuild (sigmaF 0.3) | 27% | ~50% |
| Linf input 0.9 / 1.1 x true | +91 / -40% | +74 / -28% |

The cut halves the CVL sensitivity, removes the bias from a strong dome, and makes
SPR respond faster to changes in F; its cost is a small positive bias (about +7 to
+10%) and more noise under stable F. Linf remains the dominant sensitivity.
Recommended starting value: 0.80-0.85 x Linf, fixed across fits.

## Plus group (`Lplus`) and robust likelihood (`rob_eps`)

`Lplus` pools the largest bins into one; their total still counts, their shape does
not. `rob_eps` mixes the predicted proportions with a uniform distribution, which
bounds the cost of a few fish in bins the model barely reaches (e.g.
`rob_eps = 0.001`). A plus group at or above the cut is ignored.

```{r lplus, eval = FALSE}
fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
       settings = list(CVL = 0.1, Lplus = 45, rob_eps = 0.001))
```

## GTG range: `maxsd`, `ngtg`, `tail_warning`

The largest growth group stops at $L_\infty(1 + \text{maxsd} \cdot \text{CVL})$; fish
beyond it get near-zero probability. With `maxsd = 2` (LBSPR default) the effective
CV of the groups is about 0.9 x CVL. `tail_warning = TRUE` reports how many
observed fish lie beyond the largest group. A tail cut makes this irrelevant,
because the affected bins lie far above the cut.

# Reference points, steepness and advice

## Fspr and per-recruit quantities

The fit stores Fspr for `settings$spr_ref` (default 40%), computed in TMB, so
`fspr_flicc()` and the indicators are fast. Other targets are computed on demand:

```{r refpts}
fspr_flicc(fit)                    # stored Fspr40
fspr_flicc(fit, spr = 30)          # computed
fcur_flicc(fit); sprcur_flicc(fit)
```

## From SPR to relative spawning biomass

With Beverton-Holt recruitment of steepness $s$, equilibrium depletion is

$$
\frac{B}{B_0} = \frac{4s\,\mathrm{SPR} - (1 - s)}{5s - 1},
$$

so SPR overstates depletion when $s < 1$. `spr2brel()` maps SPR to $B/B_{tgt}$ and
`flicc2FLStockR(s = )` applies it to the advice object (F is unchanged):

```{r steepness}
spr2brel(c(0.2, 0.3, 0.4), s = 0.75, sprref = 40)
stk_s <- flicc2FLStockR(fit, spr.btgt = 0.4, rel = TRUE, s = 0.75)
plot_LBAdvice(FLStocks(SPR = flicc2FLStockR(fit, rel = TRUE), relB_s0.75 = stk_s), panel = 1)
```

`eqstklen(fit, s = )` and `prbrp_flicc()` give the full equilibrium curves and
MSY proxies.

```{r eq, fig.height = 5}
eqstk <- eqstklen(fit, s = 0.75)
eqstk@refpts
```

## Length-based indicators

`LBIspr()` compares the observed proportion of large fish with the proportion
expected at Fspr; `LBImean()` compares mean lengths. Both use the fit's tail cut by
default (`tail_cut = NULL`), so indicator and likelihood use the same bins;
`tail_cut = FALSE` uses all bins, a number sets another cut.

```{r lbi}
LBIspr(fit_cut, thresh = 0.75)
attr(LBIspr(fit_cut), "Lcut")
plot_LBIspr(fit, thresh = 0.75)
```

# Population and observation model choices

| Purpose | `pop_model` | `obs_model` | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| default, LBSPR-like | `"gtg"` | `"mn"` | fast, stable |
| overdispersed compositions | `"gtg"` | `"dm"` | precision from ESS; good MSE choice |
| fishblicc-like | `"gamma"` | `"nb"` | slower |

```{r models, fig.height = 4}
fit_dm <- fiticc(lfd.ess, stklen, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"), catch_by_gear = c(0.7, 0.3),
                 settings = list(CVL = 0.1, obs_model = "dm"))
plot_spr(list(gtg_mn = fit, gtg_dm_ess = fit_dm))
```

The fishblicc Bombay duck example (three dome-shaped gears, priors on Linf, M/k
and CVL) is in the introductory vignette.

# Monte-Carlo ensembles

`mc_flicc()` refits the model for draws of the life-history parameters (Linf, k,
M, L50, CVL; correlated, FishLife-type correlations by default) and keeps each
fit's SPR, F, selectivity and log-likelihood. Each refit uses the original fit's
settings and starts from its estimates.

Practical rules:

- **Keep CVL fixed in each refit** (`CVL.sd = NULL`, the default) and let the
  ensemble vary it through the draws. A very tight prior (e.g. `CVL.sd = 0.001`)
  gives almost the same estimate but an ill-conditioned Hessian.
- **Use a tail cut.** Jumps and bimodality in the likelihood across draws come
  mainly from the GTG tail: as Linf or CVL changes, the largest group crosses
  bin boundaries and fish in those bins switch between near-zero and positive
  probability. A cut well below the largest group removes those bins; because
  `tail_cut` is a length, every draw uses the same bins. `rob_eps` is an
  alternative.
- **Use fixed sigmaF** (default) for speed; `F_re = TRUE` multiplies the run time.
- **Weight by fit, with care.** `mc_aic_weights()` weights draws by AIC; with a
  cut the likelihoods are comparable across draws.

```{r mc}
mc <- mc_flicc(fit_cut, nsim = 30, verbose = FALSE)
mean(mc$ok)
mc_spr_tab(mc, dAIC_cut = 20)
```

```{r mc-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_mcprofile(mc)
plot_mcsprdist(mc, dAIC_cut = 20)
```

# Use in an MSE

`flicc.sa()` wraps `fiticc()` as the estimation step of an `mse` management
procedure (FLR `mse` package), with `lbi.hcr()`, `rfb.flicc.hcr()` and
`flicc.is()` as harvest-control and implementation steps. Settings recommended
for speed and stability:

```{r mse, eval = FALSE}
est <- mseCtrl(method = flicc.sa, args = list(
  lhpar = lhpar, sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "logistic"),
  settings = list(obs_model = "dm", CVL = 0.1,
                  sigmaF = 0.3,        # fixed (or the F_re estimate from the real data)
                  tail_cut = 47,       # absolute length, same in every iteration
                  spr_ref = 40),       # Fspr40 stored by each fit
  spr = 40))
```

- `se = FALSE` is used inside `flicc.sa()` (no standard errors needed).
- Fixed sigmaF avoids its estimation in every year and iteration.
- The tail cut and sigmaF both trade responsiveness against stability; tune
  them together with the smoothing of the harvest control rule.
- Expect the equilibrium model to be pessimistic during a rebuild from deep
  depletion (lag plus rising recruitment) and optimistic while F increases.

# Practical recommendations

| Topic | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Model | `gtg` with `mn` (or `dm` with effective sample sizes) |
| Growth | fix Linf and CVL at the best estimates; treat Linf uncertainty as the main sensitivity |
| F over time | random walk with sigmaF fixed (0.3 default, or the `F_re` estimate) |
| Tail | `tail_cut` at about 0.80-0.85 x Linf, as a length; `rob_eps` / `Lplus` as alternatives |
| Selectivity | dome only with gear knowledge; a tail cut reduces the cost of a mild dome |
| Status | SPR at the year's F; `s` in `flicc2FLStockR()` for $B/B_{tgt}$ under Beverton-Holt |
| Ensembles | CVL fixed per draw, tail cut, fixed sigmaF |
| MSE | fixed sigmaF, absolute tail cut, `se = FALSE`; tune with the HCR |
